chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said:
No calamity befalls the servant except due to a sin, and what Allah forgives of is greater.

key_terms.الْعَبْدَ: the servant, meaning the human being before Allah
key_terms.نَكْبَةٍ: a calamity or affliction that strikes a person

ai.seo_question: Do calamities happen because of sins in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that afflictions reaching a servant are tied to sins, while also emphasizing the vastness of Allah’s pardon. Its significance lies in joining moral accountability with hope in divine forgiveness.
